Yes If yes, when were you first elected to your current office? Democrat, Working Families Party 2010 Full Name of Campaign Committee: Friends of Mike Gianaris Campaign Website: https://www.mikegianaris.com/ Campaign Twitter Account: SenGianaris Campaign Facebook Page: http://fb.com/SenGianaris If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? Yes Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE (Short Answer) Please provide brief responses to each of the following questions - cite specific examples of your policy proposals and/or previous actions as applicable. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. This past session I was happy to help pass the Gender Expression Non-Discrimination Act, which bars discrimination, harassment, and retaliation on the basis of gender identity or expression in the workplace, as well as a ban on conversion therapy. When I was first elected to the Senate, I flipped a seat held by a no-vote on marriage equality to a yes vote. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? In the Senate, I’ve helped bring about the largest Democratic majority in over a century and shepherded the historic legislative session of 2019, which was the most productive and progressive in history. Among our accomplishments was the passage of GENDA and a ban of conversion therapy, as well as the state’s strongest-ever tenant protections and new rights for our immigrant neighbors. Our work is not done, and I will continue fighting to level the playing field between the wealthy and powerful and everyday New Yorkers.

[PDF page 2] 2020 State Senate Candidate Questionnaire Responses Please detail any specific policy proposals you may have that will affect the LGBT community. In the future, I will continue to publicly support and advocate for policies that protect our LGBTQIA+ community. Section 3: STATE LEGISLATION (yes or no) Legislation and Policies SDNYC Supports: Do you support enshrining and continuing anti-discrimination protections for these classes of individuals from discrimination in all its forms: race, color, national origin, and in most cases, sex, disability, and religion? (Existing state law does not provide consistent non-discrimination protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity.) * Yes Gender Recognition Act. Provides three options for the designation of sex by applicants for driver's licenses and learner's permits. Assembly: Ortiz (A3457B), Senate: Hoylman (S56B) Yes Expanding Gender Neutral Restrooms In All Public Spaces. Relates to making all single occupancy bathrooms gender neutral in school districts, charter schools, SUNY, CUNY, community colleges, restaurants, bars, mercantile establishments, factories and state owned or operated buildings. Assembly: O'Donnell (A6500A), Senate: Salazar (S6479) Yes Gender Expression, Identity & Inclusivity Addressing Cyberbullying in Schools. Establishes a task force to explore the effects of cyber-bullying in New York state and potential measures to address such effects. Assembly: Barrett (A3057A), Senate: Kaminsky (S5786B) Yes Improving School Gender Policies. Requires the board of education and the trustees or sole trustee of every school district to establish policies and procedures regarding the treatment of transgender or gender non-conforming students. Democratic Full Name of Campaign Committee: Stradford For Senate Campaign Website: http://Stradford4Senate.com Campaign Twitter Account: Stradford2020 Campaign Facebook Page: http://BrandonStradfordForStateSenate If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? Yes Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE (Short Answer) Please provide brief responses to each of the following questions - cite specific examples of your policy proposals and/or previous actions as applicable. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. As an HR Professional, I was a lead voice in how our employment processes were not prepared for transgender workers. I worked very hard to ease the pre-employment medical process for my agency's first encounter. It was heartwrenching for me and for the candidate. I spoke to leadership to immediately protect this individual from mistreatment and shaming, and to explore how we can educate ourselves going forward. This person became a leader in LGBTQ policy, practice and more. I remain deeply committed to engage difficult conversations of disparities that prevent full diversity, equity and inclusivity for all, especially LGBTQ civil rights. I served on the first Agency Leadership Advisory Council to support and undergird the mission of the newly formed Administration for Childrens Services Office of LGBTQ Policy and Practice. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? This District is looking for Me, a leader who is PRESENT, BELIEVABLE, HONEST, READY to work for the Constituents, and is NOT a member of the IDC.

[PDF page 6] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses As the State Senate Candidate, I alone distributed a COVID platform. As COVID- 19 mercilessly sweeps through our City and through the District, our communities of color are disproportionately affected with tragic outcomes that far outnumber non-minority neighborhoods. This pandemic has exposed the systemic failure of adequate and accessible healthcare to address longtime health comorbidities among black, brown, LGBTQ and other minority populations. Tragically the death toll in New York City increases daily by the hundreds, and yet, in our densely populated neighborhoods, untold individuals succumb unreported and unknown. This isn't a new trend, I've sounded the alarm about our medically underserved District for years. Now pressed by the media, some electeds say "the disparities are real and unfortunate" ... I say it's a national disgrace! Still, healthcare access has not improved, Staten Island still has no public hospital, and there are just two testing sites in the North Shore (one by appointment only). Coney Island Hospital, fortunately, continues to serve area residents. My parents taught me and my siblings, literally, to set a table for the poor and the castaway; so we would become "Champions" for the least of us. As such, I am a fierce advocate of worker's rights, economic security, and upholding Union guarantees. I am a TRUE Democrat and an unafraid "Voice for the Voiceless". I was born and raised in the West Brighton neighborhood of Staten Island. For several years, the Edwin Markham Gardens (NYCHA) was home. "The Markham Homes" was a multicultural community of 360 working class families with dreams to thrive, and not to simply exist. For over 30 years as a Human Resources Professional, I have battled Economic Injustice, by connecting the unemployed and underemployed, Veterans, LGBTQ individuals, and Homeless or Sheltered persons, to hundreds of full time jobs. I exposed oppressive policies aimed to diminish Worker Protections and Labor Unions. In so doing, I implemented mandated Worker protection programs, and trained Managers on best practices and supervision, worker education and protections. I am very proud of my reputation as an Intermediary and Problem Solver with Management, Unions and Employees. Community Health Education: To address the disparities in both health outcomes and healthcare access across the 23rd District, I hosted, "Ask The Doctors", a community wellness forum. While a multi-purposed event, one takeaway of this expert panel of NINE Black Male Physicians, remains to excite and encourage young men of color to consider careers in medicine. The Physicians of "Ask The Doctors" are fully cognizant of the detriment caused by the barriers to access and

[PDF page 7] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses ability to pay for health care, oft-times, life saving medical care. The forums only convene in communities of color and attempt to break through the biases and microaggressions so often exhibited in many Patient/Doctor experiences. Attendees were encouraged to ask the questions that they don't or wouldn't ask, or questions that providers ignore. Tenant Association Presidents in Coney Island called ME when their community food pantries were bare, and I delivered! During President Trump's 2019 budget shutdown - which caused millions of Federal employees to work without pay, including Coast Guard servicepersons - I was honored that my Dad, an 85 year old Coast Guard Veteran, joined me to deliver a truckload of groceries to Coast Guard families stationed at Fort Wadsworth, Staten Island. As a true Leader, I know how and when to lead from within. Let me assure everyone, it's ok to serve humanity, especially the least of us. It's ok to show compassion and to show that that you really care. Please detail any specific policy proposals you may have that will affect the LGBT community. Seamless and Fearless Health and Mental Health Access! The 23rd District is Federally designated as Medically Underserved. The lack of medical access has lead to poorer health outcomes, patient fear and guilt, and even refusal by providers - especially regarding our LGBTQ neighbors. I support the New York Health program, a comprehensive and universal single-payer system of access to health insurance for ALL New York State residents. Staten Island is the only borough without a public hospital. I would legislate permanent changes to the Indigent Care Pool to insure that our safety-net hospitals remain in operation, like Richmond University Medical Center. I will fight against 2020 cuts to funding of healthcare delivery, specifically of Medicaid, which is critically vital to the health and welfare of 'the least of us', yes the marginalized Black and Brown folks, LGBTQ folks, and Seniors. [PDF page 10] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses For any 'no' answer above, please explain: Comprehensive Sexuality Education. Grades K-5: I question just how age appropriate this curriculum can be based on the topic specific benchmarks noted in the National Sexuality Education Standard. Advisory oversight and public availability of the curriculum, as included in the Bill, shouldn't supercede the will of the parents and school community. I do support this curriculum for grades 6-12 without hesitation. More clearly, the religious institution would need to bring (or store) everything needed for the service, set it up, break it down, and exit. No If yes, when were you first elected to your current office? Democrat Full Name of Campaign Committee: Jason Salmon for New York Campaign Website: http://salmon4ny.com Campaign Twitter Account: JasonASalmon Campaign Facebook Page: http://www.facebook.com/Salmon4NY If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? Yes Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE (Short Answer) Please provide brief responses to each of the following questions - cite specific examples of your policy proposals and/or previous actions as applicable. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. I am a member of Lambda Independent Democrats and Stonewall Democrats and attend many of their meetings and events as well as the Jim Owles club. I support LGBTQ+ civil and social rights and see the LGBTQ+ community as being an integral part of the American fabric and Senate District 25. Regarding issues that face the LGBTQ+ community that I now support and will actively advocate for as a legislator is, the decriminalization of sex work, repealing the “Walking While Trans Statute, passing the gender recognition act, and focusing on providing safe spaces for LGBTQ+ youth, which includes housing, mental health services and educational opportunities. Importantly, LGBTQ+ elders will always be included in my advocacy. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? I am a life-long resident of the 25th District 25 which I seek to represent in the NYS Senate.I was born and raised in the district. I have a demonstrated commitment to the district and to everyday New Yorkers. I am in the unique position to bring

[PDF page 12] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses diverse populations to the table to create an inclusive campaign, centered around racial and economic justice. I am a progressive Democrat whose family history in the district dates back 70 years. My ancestors, Black, White, Jewish, Christian, and Muslim, immigrated to the U.S., as have so many, in search of economic opportunities and for some to escape religious and political persecution. I am acutely aware of the sacrifices both my distant and near ancestors made to reach the United States and I am dedicated to ensuring this country remains a haven for those in need. From an early age I was inspired by music, I am a classically trained violinist and after graduating college I turned my love for music into a career becoming the owner of a recording studio. I worked with many talented, Brooklyn-based artists. However, in the summer of 2014, my life changed dramatically. While we all watched the death of Eric Garner with anger and frustration, one of my childhood friends was killed by the police. He was a gentle and kind human being who joined the Air Force after high school. He served for eight years, only to return home to lose his life at the hands of the police. These tragedies drove me to become a community organizer and activist. I volunteered for Jews for Racial and Economic Justice (JFREJ), serving as their liaison to Communities United for Police Reform. As an activist and community organizer I assisted to organize support for legislation that strengthened transparency and accountability for law enforcement including the Right to Know Act and the Police State Act. I am also a co-founder of JFREJ’s “Jews of Color” group. I went on to work for Senator Velmanette Montgomery (25thDistrict) as a Community Liaison where for nearly three years I was on the front lines serving the communities of the 25th District. From fighting for affordable housing to forming partnerships between city and state agencies and the community, to assisting NYCHA residents get needed repairs, I helped craft practical solutions to the district’s everyday problems. I have been on the front lines fighting for affordable housing and tenant rights as a vocal opponent of socially irresponsible developments that put profits over our community. I have helped tenants organize to demand repairs to their apartments and worked with local elected officials to draft legislation that promotes civics education in our schools.

[PDF page 13] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses Today, I am running on a platform centered around ending mass incarceration, addressing the affordable housing crisis, fighting for equity in our education system and ending the rampant social and economic chasm plaguing our society. My professional experience as both a community organizer and staffer for Senator Montgomer has provided me with a dual lens and experience- understanding the community I seek to represent along with the knowledge how bills get passed in Albany. Both provide me with the foundation to be an effective legislator and advocate for everyday New Yorkers in Albany. Please detail any specific policy proposals you may have that will affect the LGBT community. In the wake of the recent SCOTUS case addressing employment protections for LGBTQ+ communities we must redouble our efforts to continue the fight to protect and recognize the hard-won rights of the LGBTQ+ community. GENDA, a long fought-for law passed by the NYS Legislature in 2019, added gender identity and expression to the State’s human rights and hate laws and recognizes LGBTQ+ as a protected class. GENDA now prohibits discrimination in employment, housing, and public accommodations against the LGBTQ+ community. Now we must ensure that our government services and protections match these values and strengthen the law as we see weaknesses and loopholes in it that require closing. I will work closely with the LGBTQ+ community and advocacy organizations to craft regulations and legislation to make sure the promises of GENDA are kept. Since Trump took office there's been a significant uptick in violence against members of the transgender and gender non-conforming violence (TGNC) which disproportionately affects trans women of color. We need to ensure the State recognizes and validates these identities and provide a safer and braver space for New Yorkers to be themselves. If elected I will be a strong advocate for legislation that protects the LGBTQ+ community. State protections are increasingly important in the “Age of Trump'' where our federal courts are compromised by appointments of unqualified judges who are openly hostile to the LGBTQ+ community. The 77th precinct, which is in my district, has one of the highest rates of arrests for “Walking While Trans” in all of New York. I will not only prioritize passing legislation to repeal the “Walking While Trans” ban, but I will introduce legislation that enables those with prior

[PDF page 14] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses violations for Loitering for the Purpose of Prostitution violations and convictions to clear their records so that they can access employment. If elected, I will also work to decriminalize sex work. I recognize the disproportionate impact the criminal justice system can have on LGBTQ+ people, and I will push to restore recent bail reforms that were rolled back in the recent budget so that people like Layleen Polanco will not be unjustly incarcerated. Finally, I will vote in favor of legalizing surrogacy with protections for all participants. I am also concerned about LGBTQ+ youth who are disproportionately homeless or have to be removed from foster homes for abusive treatment. Despite the fact that New York has comprehensive legal protections (N.Y. Comp. Codes R. & Regs. tit. 14, § 527.8(d) and N.Y. Comp. Codes R. & Regs. tit. 11, § 52.16(2) in place to protect LGBTQI youth, 78% of homeless LBGTQ+ youth who have either run away or were removed from their homes report abuse and unacceptable treatment by the foster family. In the 2017 study, Safe Havens: Closing the Gap Between Recommended Practice and Reality for Transgender and Gender-Expansive Youth in Out-of-Home Care,” the Children’s Rights organization recommends that not only do we need legal and policy protections to encourage positive staff hiring, training and coaching practices, but we must also provide, “better support for families of origin and foster and adoptive parents; increased community collaboration; intentional engagement with LGBTQ+ young people to ensure that they are affirmed in care; and a commitment to agency-wide culture change” (Children’s Rights). The traditional model of gender separation does not work for a community of individuals who do not identify with a gender binary. LGBTQ+ youth need safe spaces that affirm their identity, with resource centers for runaway youth as well as for those struggling at home or in foster care. As a priority, these centers should support helping homeless youth get documentation so they can sign up for government services like Medicaid, provide public transportation access like metrocards, as well as appropriate physical and mental health services, crisis stabilization services, addiction treatment services or referrals (I support housing first), transitional housing, GED, Get College Ready, and skills/trade counselors and educators to help with educational and employment opportunities. These centers should re-create the type of supportive, home-like environment, like the model of the Ali Forney Center in NYC, to properly serve our youth. As a legislator I would want to work with advocacy groups and the experts in this field to devise new requirements such as foster family and supporting professionals

[PDF page 15] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses training along with other support systems that affirm this at-risk, vulnerable community. As a state legislator I would make it my mission to ensure that these youths are provided with the necessary resources and funding they need. Yes Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE (Short Answer) Please provide brief responses to each of the following questions - cite specific examples of your policy proposals and/or previous actions as applicable. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. If elected, I’d be the first openly gay state senator in Brooklyn, and the first openly gay state senator of color in all New York. I extensively lobbied, marched, and phonebanked for marriage equality in NY, both during the 2009 vote and the 2011 vote (when we won!). What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? My family’s lived in Prospect Heights (the center of the district) for three generations - this is my community and I know its struggles. In 2017, when I ran for City Council in the overlapping neighborhoods, I earned the votes of over 9,000 people in these neighborhoods, despite running on an independent line. Members of my community agreed with our vision of a transparent and responsive government at all levels that serves all the people, and isn’t afraid to speak truth to power. I’ve marched with these people, been arrested while protesting with them,

[PDF page 19] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses and had more conversations than I can count over the years. I’m ready to fight for them in Albany. Please detail any specific policy proposals you may have that will affect the LGBT community. The issues that most seriously affect the LGBTQ community are homelessness, job discrimination, and access to competent healthcare including competent healthcare. In addition, the most vulnerable members of our community are subject to violence by police and others, while their basic means of maintaining a living are criminalized. These major structural programs have to be addressed by aggressive reform. I believe that queer legislators have a responsibility to talk about solutions to the problems facing our community, for example talking about how expanding healthcare access expands access to PReP and other HIV treatment, or talking about access to hormones for transgender people could be significantly expanded unders such a system. No one should have to go to Callen-Lorde or APICHA and find themselves turned away due to capacity and drug shortages. We need to expand mental health access, offer more affordable housing to keep our youth out of shelters and off the streets when they are kicked out of their homes, and expand access to good jobs. I also think we need to build movements and stand steadfast against police violence, and that especially means fighting things like the “Walking While Trans” Ban and ending the criminalization of sex workers. I will also support Senate Bill S56B, which ensures that all New Yorkers, including transgender and non-binary New Yorkers, can get identity documents, like passports and birth certificates, that align with their gender identity. I am a movement candidate, and I will fight every day I’m in office to make this happen. In New York State, when the Democrats took control of the New York State Senate for the first real time in almost 100 years, we made significant strides in establishing basic protections for the LGBT community. First and foremost, we passed GENDA to prohibit discrimination on the basis of gender identity or expression and included gender identity and expression under hate crime law. GENDA was especially important because we added Transgender New Yorkers to those protected by the state’s Hate Crime Laws. In addition to passing GENDA, we passed a ban on conversion therapy,which was the morally and ethically next right thing to do, prohibiting mental health professionals from engaging in sexual orientation change efforts with a patient under the age of eighteen. I also am advocating for including a third gender option on state documents. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? As the democratic incumbent for the 34th state senate district, representing the Bronx & Westchester in Albany for the past 14 months, I realize that the most important core value that I carry with me into every meeting, event, and session on the floor is integrity and transparency. We have failed in almost every category when it comes to putting New Yorkers first. If we actually want to earn the title of public servants, we must start serving the public instead of the special interests who have been given the key to the castle for far too long. Yes, we’ve made progress on LGBT issues, housing issues, criminal justice reform, immigration issues, election reform, reproductive rights, sexual harassment, assault and rape laws, however, let us not be jaded or blinded by the progress we’ve made. Progress that was stalled for a decade, and progress that only brought us “current” so to speak. As we look towards the future, it is incumbent upon us to have a collective vision that brings New York forward, and let’s New York lead to its fullest potential. To do so requires embracing technology and the future of work, upending racism, sexism, and homophobia. Becoming a state where all zip codes are desirable to live in because the air is clean and the schools are good. Sure. We have made progress, but we have not taken the necessary step forward to lead. I am running for re-election to continue the work I have set out to accomplish in the New York State Senate, and to see the above mentioned vision to fruition. My desire to serve and my dedication to do what is right and just has only grown more deeply in my 14 months serving; and as Chairwoman of the Ethics Committee, my work is certainly far from done. I believe that our time as legislators is precious. We have an unknown amount of time serving, just like we have an unknown amount of time on this earth. That means that every issue I stand by, and every issue I fight for, is done with intense passion and urgency, because no one knows what tomorrow will bring. While serving, I have experienced some of the most disappointing days in my life -- but these days have often been followed by utter inspiration, motivation and a fervor to break down the walls erected to keep certain people, ideas, and laws alive. I believe these walls were made to be taken down by me, and my commitment to justice and a world that is equally accessible to everyone, has only grown stronger and louder during this time.
